facts.statement: Congosaurus fossils were discovered in Lândana, Angola, and date to the Paleocene epoch.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from Lândana, in Angola and date back to the Paleocene epoch.

facts.statement: A new species, C. compressus, was established in 2007 after being previously classified under the genus Rhabdognathus.
facts.quote: In 2007, a new species of Congosaurus was constructed after previously being assigned to Rhabdognathus, and named C. compressus

facts.statement: Congosaurus is classified as an extinct genus of dyrosaurid mesoeucrocodylian.
facts.quote: Congosaurus is an extinct genus of dyrosaurid mesoeucrocodylian.

facts.statement: The genus Congosaurus belongs to the family Dyrosauridae.
Between 1952 and 1964, Congosaurus was proposed to be synonymous with the genus Dyrosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1952 and 1964 Congosaurus was proposed to be synonymous with Dyrosaurus.

facts.statement: In 1976 and 1980, the genus Congosaurus was considered synonymous with Hyposaurus.
facts.quote: The genus was later thought synonymous with Hyposaurus in 1976 and 1980.

facts.statement: The lateromedially compressed teeth of Congosaurus indicate a close relationship to the species C. bequaerti.
facts.quote: Lateromedially compressed teeth show its close relation to C. bequaerti.

facts.statement: The parent group for Congosaurus is the subfamily Hyposaurinae.
Congosaurus lived from the Danian to the Ypresian stages, approximately 66 to 48.07 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Danian to Ypresian (66 to 48.07 million years ago)

rejected.quote: A potential third, but indeterminate species of Congosaurus has been reported from Eocene-aged Cambay Shale Formation of Gujarat, India.
